defs.def: to have or keep an image in your memory of an event, a person, a place, etc. from the past 回想起；记得；记起

ex.s: As far as I can remember, I’ve always been a night owl.
ex.t: 据我所记，我一直是个夜猫子。

ex.s: Mum is small, but I remember feeling so high up there.
ex.t: 妈妈个子很小，但我记得在那里感觉好高啊。

ex.s: —Do you remember little Julien from Grade Two?
ex.t: ——你还记得二年级的小朱利安吗？

ex.s: This form of remembered contact with a book can accompany us during a lifetime and continue to strengthen and shape us.
ex.t: 这种带着记忆的与书接触的方式可以陪伴我们一生，并持续地强化和塑造我们。

ex.s: I do remember, though, what it was like to be a complete beginner.
ex.t: 不过，我确实记得作为一个彻头彻尾的初学者是什么感觉。

ex.s: I remember showing my parents a video of Bea Johnson, sharing how cool I thought it would be to buy groceries with jars, and have so little trash!
ex.t: 我记得给父母看了一段比阿·约翰逊的视频，分享我认为用罐子买杂货、产生极少垃圾会是多么酷！

ex.s: I was stupid with cold, but I couldn’t remember the last time I’d felt so happy.
ex.t: 我冻得傻乎乎的，但我记不起上次感到这么快乐是什么时候了。

ex.s: Research has found that learning obtained from a well-told story is remembered more accurately, and for far longer, than from facts and figures.
ex.t: 研究发现，从一个讲述精彩的故事中学到的东西，比从事实和数据中学到的记得更准确，也持久得多。

ex.s: Older people today, for example, can remember a time with insect-covered car windscreens after long drives.
ex.t: 例如，如今的老年人还能记得长途驾驶后车窗上沾满昆虫的时代。

ex.s: “I remember the first time I saw a humpback whale; it just rose out of the water like some prehistoric creature and I thought it was smiling at us.
ex.t: “我记得第一次看到座头鲸的时候，它就像某种史前生物一样从水中升起，我觉得它在对着我们微笑。

ex.s: I have for as long as I can remember.
ex.t: 从我能记事起就是这样。

ex.s: I remember the first really   48   customer we had at Covent Garden.
ex.t: 我记得我们在Covent Garden遇到的第一个真正   48  的顾客。

ex.s: I remember her reading a magazine while taking the part of the Wolf in a game of “Little Red Riding Hood” with my brother’s two daughters.
ex.t: 我记得她一边读杂志，一边和我哥哥的两个女儿玩“小红帽”游戏，扮演大灰狼。

ex.s: I remember the day shyness took over my life.
ex.t: 我记得害羞占据我生活的那一天。

ex.s: I still remember   59   (visit) a friend who’d lived here for five years and I   60  (shock) when I learnt she hadn’t cooked once in all that time.
ex.t: 我还记得___59___（visit）一位在这里住了五年的朋友，当我得知她那段时间一次饭都没做过时，我___60___（shock）。

ex.s: I still remember how hard first day was.
ex.t: 我仍然记得第一天有多难。

ex.s: I remember when you were his age, you said that you wanted to be a professional football player.
ex.t: 我记得当你在他这个年纪的时候，你说过你想成为一名职业足球运动员。

ex.s: I must have always known reading was very important because the first memories I have as a child deal with books． There was not one night that I don't remember mom reading me a storybook by my bedside． I was extremely inspired by the elegant way the words sounded．
ex.t: 我一定一直都知道阅读非常重要，因为我童年最早的记忆都与书有关。没有哪个夜晚我不记得妈妈在床边给我读故事书。那些文字优雅的读音极大地启发了我。

ex.s: My nature-loving friends had remembered to bring all the necessities of life.
ex.t: 我热爱自然的朋友们记得带上所有生活必需品。

ex.s: Then I would try to remember the different possessions I supposedly had taken away—since I seldom actually kept them.
ex.t: 然后我会试着记起我假想中被拿走的不同财物——因为我其实很少真的留下它们。

ex.s: —Next time you visit Bob, remember to give him a call in advance.
ex.t: —下次你去看鲍勃，记得提前给他打个电话。

ex.s: If you don’t understand what you’re reading, how would you remember it?
ex.t: 如果你不理解你正在读的内容，又怎么能记得住呢？

defs.def: to bring back to your mind a fact, piece of information, etc. that you knew 想起；记起

ex.s: Para1:  The next day we remembered the brand-new tent we had brought with us.
ex.t: 第1段：第二天，我们想起了随身带来的那顶崭新帐篷。

ex.s: I remember back to my 7th year in school.
ex.t: 到了17英里处，我已经上气不接下气，曾经受伤的脚踝剧烈疼痛。

defs.def: to keep an important fact in your mind 记住；把 … 牢记在心

ex.s: However, psychologists have demonstrated that when adults read news stories, they remember more of the content than if they listen to or view identical pieces.
ex.t: 然而，心理学家已经证明，当成年人阅读新闻故事时，比起聆听或观看相同的片段，他们对内容的记忆更多。

ex.s: They are more likely to remember people’s mistakes.
ex.t: 他们更容易记住人们的错误。

ex.s: Whatever the mistake, remember it isn’t a fixed aspect of your personality.
ex.t: 无论犯了什么错，记住它不是你性格中固定不变的一面。

ex.s: So a music teacher may find the addition of deliberate errors could help a student remember the right musical notes.
ex.t: 因此，一位音乐老师可能会发现，加入故意的错误有助于学生记住正确的音符。

ex.s: Remember, it's a party!
ex.t: 记住，这是个派对！

ex.s: Remember, even world champion athletes practice their skills on a consistent basis.
ex.t: 记住，即使是世界冠军运动员也在持续练习他们的技能。

ex.s: Remember, your doctor and other caregivers are on your side.
ex.src: 2020全国新高考II卷·Talking with your doctor
ex.t: 带上你的病历，包括你当前用药的清单。

ex.s: But remember, it’s you that has to grow and read and reread in order to better understand your friends.
ex.t: 但请记住，是你自己需要成长、阅读和反复阅读，才能更好地理解你的朋友。

ex.s: Remember, you are only human.
ex.t: 记住，你只是凡人。

ex.s: Remember that Thomas Costain was 57 when he published his first novel, and that Grandma Moses showed her first pictures when she was 78.
ex.t: 记住，托马斯·科斯坦57岁时才出版了他的第一部小说，而摩西奶奶78岁时才展出了她的第一批画作。

ex.s: However you start, remember there is no better time to start than right now, for you'll never be more alive than you are at this moment.
ex.t: 无论你如何开始，记住没有比现在更好的开始时间，因为你再也不会比此刻更有活力了。

ex.s: Remember that goals are flexible.
ex.t: 记住目标是灵活的。

ex.s: But it's worth remembering that the banking system that we now all live with is just that: A modern invention.
ex.t: 但值得记住的是，我们现在赖以生存的银行体系不过如此：一种现代发明。

ex.s: How to Remember What You Read
ex.t: 如何记住你所读的内容

ex.s: But the next step is making sure that you remember what you’ve read!
ex.t: 有些书，你立刻就会产生共鸣。

ex.s: Here are a few tricks for remembering what you read.
ex.t: 这里有几个帮助你记住所读内容的技巧。

ex.s: If the plot, characters, or word usage is confusing for you, likely won’t be able to remember what you read.
ex.t: 如果情节、人物或用词让你困惑，你很可能记不住读过什么。

ex.s: If you read frequently, you’ll likely have and easier time with remembering what you’re reading(and what you’ve read).
ex.t: 如果你经常阅读，你可能会更容易记住你正在读的内容（以及你已经读过的内容）。

ex.s: You’ll learn to enjoy literature—as you remember what you read!
ex.t: 你会学会欣赏文学——同时记住你所读的内容！

ex.s: Then, they will introduce their supporting arguments with expressions such as We must remember that… and We can’t deny that… Student A: Turn to Page 83.
ex.t: 然后，他们会用“我们必须记住……”和“我们不能否认……”这样的表达引出支撑论点。学生A：翻到第83页。

ex.s: Marking helps you remember what you read.
ex.t: 标记有助于你记住所读的内容。

ex.s: "One thing to remember is that it's the process not the end product that matters."
ex.t: “要记住的一点是，重要的是过程，而不是最终产品。”

ex.s: This will help you understand and remember the information you hear.
ex.t: 这将帮助你理解并记住你听到的信息。

ex.s: Remember important dates
ex.t: 记住重要的日期。

ex.s: Writing down what the doctor says will help you remember important information.
ex.src: 2020全国新高考II卷·Talking with your doctor
ex.t: 把医生说的话写下来会帮助你记住重要信息。

ex.s: Remember the saying: on the Internet, nobody knows you're a dog.
ex.t: 记住那句名言：在互联网上，没人知道你是一条狗。

ex.s: Storytelling helps with learning also because stories are easy to remember.
ex.t: 讲故事也有助于学习，因为故事容易记住。

defs.def: to not forget to do sth; to actually do what you have to do 记着，不忘（去做）；动手做（必须做的事）
to think about sb with respect, especially when saying a prayer 纪念；缅怀；思念

ex.s: To remember a writer.
ex.t: 为了纪念一位作家。

ex.s: To remember a great writer.
ex.t: 为了纪念一位伟大的作家。

ex.s: To remember the birth of jazz.
ex.t: 为了纪念爵士乐的诞生。

ex.s: To remember a friend.
ex.t: 为了纪念一位朋友。

ex.s: To remember a friend.
ex.t: 为了纪念一位朋友。

ex.s: Don’t forget to stop by Pacific Science Center’s Store while you are here to pick up a wonderful science activity or remember your visit.
ex.t: 在此期间，别忘了顺道去太平洋科学中心的商店，挑选一项精彩的科学活动或纪念品来纪念你的参观。

defs.def: to give money, a present, etc. to sb/sth 给 … 送钱（或礼品等）
